say.text: Salah ad-Din loved to hear the traditions told, and when he was at Alexandria, he often visited the scholar al-Hafiz al-Silafi, and learned a great number from him. Ibn Shaddad says so.
Shawar's men are in sight of the south wall, and you come to me to hear traditions? Have you no better use for your hour, young emir?
I have a great deal else to do. I will do it better for having sat here.
Then sit. The wall has stood a long time, and it can stand an hour.
Years later, Ibn Shaddad would see Salah ad-Din moved to tears by a tradition that taught something. He was a man who would go himself to find a scholar who did not come to courts.
